marking_schemes.scheme_text: Lubricates surface of eye, washes away dust, kill germs, keeps surface of eye moist, lysozyme kills bacteria.
marking_schemes.model_answer: Tears lubricate the surface of the eye, wash away dust, keep the surface moist, and contain lysozyme which kills bacteria.
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: This was correctly answered by most candidates.

marking_schemes.question_text: State the main functions of the following: Coronary Artery
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Supplies oxygenated blood to the walls of the heart.
key_points: to the walls of the heart
marking_schemes.model_answer: The coronary artery supplies oxygenated blood to the walls of the heart.
common_errors: Did not specify oxygenated blood
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Most candidates wrote incomplete answers. They did not specify oxygenated blood.

marking_schemes.question_text: State the main functions of the following: Seminal Vesicles
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Activates sperms, forms a medium for transportation of sperms.
key_points: forms medium for transportation of sperms
marking_schemes.model_answer: Seminal vesicles activate sperms and form a medium for transportation of sperms.
common_errors: Writing the function of testis instead of seminal vesicles
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Majority of the candidates wrote the correct answer. A few wrote the function of testis instead of seminal vesicles.

marking_schemes.question_text: The diagram given below represents an organ system in the human body (kidneys, ureters, urinary bladder, sphincter, urethra). Identify the system.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Excretory system/Urinary system
marking_schemes.model_answer: Excretory system / Urinary system
common_errors: Writing 'Urinogenital system'
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Most candidates identified the system correctly. 'Urinogenital system' was written as an incorrect answer by a few candidates.

marking_schemes.question_text: The diagram given below represents an organ system in the human body. Label the parts marked 2 and 4. Mention the function of part 5.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: 2 – Ureter; 4 – Sphincter; 5 – Expels urine
marking_schemes.model_answer: Part 2 – Ureter; Part 4 – Sphincter; Function of Part 5 (urethra) – Expels urine from the body.
common_errors: Labelling part 4 as urethra instead of sphincter
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Most candidates labelled part 2 and 4 and mentioned the function of part 5 correctly. However, a few did not study the diagram carefully and labelled part 4 as urethra.

marking_schemes.question_text: The diagram given below represents an organ system in the human body. Name the structural and functional units of the part marked 1 (kidney).
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Nephrons
marking_schemes.model_answer: Nephrons
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: This part of the question was answered correctly by most candidates.

marking_schemes.question_text: The diagram given below represents an organ system in the human body. What is the fluid that accumulates in part 3 (urinary bladder)? Which is the main nitrogenous waste present in it?
marking_schemes.correct_answer: Fluid: Urine; Main nitrogenous waste: Urea
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Urine; Urea
marking_schemes.model_answer: The fluid is Urine. The main nitrogenous waste present in it is Urea.
common_errors: Could not name the main nitrogenous waste (urea)
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Majority of the candidates wrote the name of the fluid correctly. However, some candidates could not mention the main nitrogenous waste present in urine.

marking_schemes.question_text: The diagram given below represents an organ system in the human body. Draw a neat, labelled diagram showing the longitudinal section of part 1 (kidney).
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Diagram showing longitudinal section of kidney with labels: Cortex, Medulla, Renal artery, Renal vein, Nephron, Ureter. (Any other correct labelling)
marking_schemes.model_answer: Draw a longitudinal section of the kidney labelling: Cortex (outer), Medulla (inner), Renal artery, Renal vein, Nephron, and Ureter.
common_errors: Could not show clear differentiation between renal cortex and medulla
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: The longitudinal section of part 1 was drawn correctly by most candidates. However, a few candidates could not show a clear differentiation between renal cortex and medulla.

marking_schemes.question_text: The diagram given below represents an endocrine gland in the human body (showing infundibulum, posterior lobe, anterior lobe). Identify the endocrine gland. Where is it located?
marking_schemes.correct_answer: Pituitary gland; Located hanging from hypothalamus
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Pituitary gland; Hangs from hypothalamus
marking_schemes.model_answer: The gland is the Pituitary gland. It hangs from the hypothalamus (in the brain).
common_errors: Could not give exact location of the gland
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Most candidates identified the endocrine gland correctly. However, a large number of candidates could not give the exact location of the gland.

marking_schemes.question_text: The diagram given below represents the pituitary gland. Why is the above gland referred to as the 'Master gland'?
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Controls the secretions of other endocrine glands/regulates the activities of other endocrine glands.
key_points: controls/regulates secretions of other endocrine glands
marking_schemes.model_answer: The pituitary gland is called the 'Master gland' because it controls the secretions and regulates the activities of other endocrine glands.
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Most candidates answered this subpart correctly.

marking_schemes.question_text: The diagram given below represents the pituitary gland. Name the hormone which in deficiency causes Diabetes Insipidus. How does this disorder differ from Diabetes Mellitus?
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Vasopressin / ADH; Diabetes mellitus is due to deficiency of insulin / high level of sugar in blood, urine has sugar. Diabetes insipidus: Normal sugar in blood, urine free of sugar / urine loaded with water.
key_points: Diabetes mellitus: deficiency of insulin / high sugar in blood / sugar in urine
Diabetes insipidus: normal blood sugar / no sugar in urine / urine loaded with water
marking_schemes.model_answer: The hormone is Vasopressin (ADH). Diabetes mellitus is due to deficiency of insulin with high blood sugar and sugar in urine. Diabetes insipidus has normal blood sugar but urine is free of sugar and loaded with water.
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: This subpart was attempted well by most candidates.

marking_schemes.question_text: The diagram given below represents the pituitary gland. Explain the term 'Hormone'. What is the role of Tropic hormones in the human body?
marking_schemes.scheme_text: It is the secretion of an endocrine gland, which is transported by blood and acts on target organs or cells. Secreted by pituitary gland and stimulates other endocrine glands to secrete their hormones.
key_points: acts on target organs or cells
tropic hormones: secreted by pituitary / stimulate other endocrine glands
marking_schemes.model_answer: A hormone is the secretion of an endocrine gland that is transported by blood and acts on target organs or cells. Tropic hormones are secreted by the pituitary gland and stimulate other endocrine glands to secrete their own hormones.
common_errors: Could not give the role of Tropic hormones
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Majority of the candidates explained the term 'Hormone' correctly but were unable to give the role of Tropic hormones in the human body.

marking_schemes.question_text: The diagram given below represents the pituitary gland. Which lobe of the above gland secretes: 1. Oxytocin 2. ACTH 3. Growth hormone
marking_schemes.correct_answer: 1 – Posterior / neurohypophysis; 2 – Anterior / adenohypophysis; 3 – Anterior / adenohypophysis
marking_schemes.scheme_text: 1 – Posterior/ neurohypophysis; 2 – Anterior / adenohypophysis; 3 – Anterior /adenohypophysis
marking_schemes.model_answer: 1. Oxytocin – Posterior lobe (neurohypophysis); 2. ACTH – Anterior lobe (adenohypophysis); 3. Growth hormone – Anterior lobe (adenohypophysis)
common_errors: Uncertain of which hormones are secreted by which lobe
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Many candidates wrote incorrect answers as they were uncertain of the hormones secreted by the two lobes of the Pituitary gland.

marking_schemes.question_text: Given below is an apparatus which was set up to investigate a physiological process in plants (bell jar, water drops, plant in a pot enclosed in rubber sheet, vaseline on glass plate). The setup was placed in bright sunlight. Name the process being studied. Define the process.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Transpiration. It is the loss of water as water vapour from the aerial parts of the plant.
key_points: loss of water as water vapour
from aerial parts of the plant
marking_schemes.model_answer: The process is Transpiration. It is the loss of water as water vapour from the aerial parts of the plant.
common_errors: Writing Photosynthesis instead of Transpiration
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Most candidates answered correctly. However, a few wrote Photosynthesis instead of Transpiration.

marking_schemes.question_text: Given below is an apparatus set up to investigate transpiration in plants. Why was the pot enclosed in a rubber sheet?
marking_schemes.scheme_text: To prevent evaporation of water from the pot/ soil.
key_points: to prevent evaporation of water from the pot / soil
marking_schemes.model_answer: The pot was enclosed in a rubber sheet to prevent evaporation of water from the pot/soil.
common_errors: Writing that transpiration occurs in soil, which is incorrect
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Few candidates could attempt this subpart correctly. Most of them wrote that transpiration occurs in soil, which is incorrect.

marking_schemes.question_text: Given below is an apparatus set up to investigate transpiration in plants. Mention two external factors which can accelerate the above process.
marking_schemes.correct_answer: Any two of: Bright sunlight / high temperature / high velocity of wind / low humidity
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Bright sunlight, high temperature, high velocity of wind, low humidity.
marking_schemes.model_answer: Two external factors that accelerate transpiration: (1) Bright sunlight / high temperature (2) High velocity of wind / low humidity
common_errors: Failed to mention intensity/degree of the factors
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Though most candidates wrote the external factors, they failed to mention their intensity which will accelerate the process.

marking_schemes.question_text: Given below is an apparatus set up to investigate transpiration in plants. List two adaptations in plants to reduce the above process.
marking_schemes.correct_answer: Any two of: Thick cuticle / loss of leaves / narrow leaves / fewer stomata / sunken stomata / leaves modified into spines / multiple layers of epidermal cells
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Thick cuticle, loss of leaves, narrow leaves, fewer stomata, sunken stomata, leaves modified into spines, multiple layers of epidermal cells.
key_points: loss of leaves / leaves modified into spines
marking_schemes.model_answer: Two adaptations: (1) Thick cuticle (2) Sunken stomata / fewer stomata / leaves modified into spines
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Majority of the candidates listed the two adaptations in plants correctly.

marking_schemes.question_text: Given below is an apparatus set up to investigate transpiration in plants. Draw a neat, labelled diagram of a stomatal apparatus.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Diagram showing stomatal apparatus with labels: Stoma, Chloroplast, Guard cell, Nucleus, Epidermal cell.
marking_schemes.model_answer: Draw the stomatal apparatus showing two kidney-shaped guard cells with the stoma (pore) between them. Label: Stoma, Guard cell (with chloroplasts and nucleus), Epidermal cell.
common_errors: Not drawing epidermal cells surrounding the guard cells
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Few candidates drew a neat, labelled diagram of a stomatal apparatus. Most candidates did not draw epidermal cells surrounding the guard cells.

marking_schemes.question_text: Given below are two stages in the evolution of man (A and B). Identify Australopithecus and Neanderthal man from the above pictures.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: A – Neanderthal man; B – Australopithecus
marking_schemes.model_answer: A – Neanderthal man; B – Australopithecus
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Most candidates identified the pictures correctly.

marking_schemes.question_text: Given below are two stages in the evolution of man. Mention two characteristic features each for the two stages (A – Neanderthal man; B – Australopithecus).
marking_schemes.scheme_text: A – absolute bipedalism, large head, broad, flat, sloping forehead, less hair on body, large cranial capacity 1,500 cm3. B – Protruding face, Chin absent, prominent eyebrow ridges, flat nose, projecting face, cranial capacity (450-600 cm3). (Any other correct characteristic feature.)
key_points: A (Neanderthal): absolute bipedalism / large cranial capacity 1500 cm3 / broad flat sloping forehead / less hair
B (Australopithecus): protruding face / chin absent / prominent eyebrow ridges / cranial capacity 450-600 cm3
marking_schemes.model_answer: A (Neanderthal man): Absolute bipedalism, large cranial capacity (~1500 cm3), broad flat sloping forehead, less hair on body. B (Australopithecus): Protruding face, chin absent, prominent eyebrow ridges, cranial capacity 450–600 cm3.
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Most candidates wrote the two characteristic features each for the two stages correctly.

marking_schemes.question_text: Given below are two stages in the evolution of man. Who proposed the theory of 'Natural Selection'?
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Charles Darwin
marking_schemes.model_answer: Charles Darwin
common_errors: Writing Lamarck instead of Darwin
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Many candidates were unsure of the name of the scientist who proposed Natural Selection. They wrote Lamarck instead of Darwin.

marking_schemes.question_text: Given below are two stages in the evolution of man. Name the organism used as an example to explain 'Industrial Melanism'.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Peppered moth / Biston betularia
marking_schemes.model_answer: Peppered moth (Biston betularia)
common_errors: Could not write the common name or scientific name
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Most candidates could not write the common name or scientific name of the organism.

marking_schemes.question_text: Given below are two stages in the evolution of man. Give two examples of Vestigial organs in humans.
marking_schemes.correct_answer: Any two of: Pinna of ear, wisdom teeth, vermiform appendix, coccyx or tailbone, arrector pili, plica semilunaris, body hair, male nipples
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Pinna of ear, wisdom teeth, vermiform appendix, coccyx or tailbone, arrector pili, plica semilunaris, body hair, male nipples.
key_points: any two: pinna of ear / wisdom teeth / vermiform appendix / coccyx / arrector pili / plica semilunaris / body hair / male nipples
marking_schemes.model_answer: Two examples of vestigial organs in humans: (1) Vermiform appendix (2) Coccyx (tailbone)
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Most candidates wrote the two examples of Vestigial organs in humans correctly.

marking_schemes.question_text: In Mendel's experiments, tall pea plants (T) are dominant over dwarf pea plants (t). What is the phenotype and genotype of the F1 generation if a homozygous tall plant is crossed with a homozygous dwarf plant?
marking_schemes.correct_answer: Phenotype – all are tall plants; Genotype – All are hybrid / heterozygous dominant (Tt)
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Phenotype – all are tall plants; Genotype – All are hybrid / heterozygous dominant
marking_schemes.model_answer: Phenotype: All plants are tall. Genotype: All are Tt (heterozygous dominant / hybrid).
common_errors: Mentioned shapes of seed and position of flower instead of height of plant
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Most candidates answered correctly. However, a few mentioned shapes of seed and position of flower instead of height of plant.

marking_schemes.question_text: In Mendel's experiments, tall pea plants (T) are dominant over dwarf pea plants (t). Draw a Punnett square board to show the gametes and offspring when both the parents are heterozygous for tallness.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Punnett square: Parents Tt x Tt; Gametes T, t from each parent; Offspring: TT, Tt, Tt, tt
key_points: gametes T and t from each parent
marking_schemes.model_answer: Punnett square for Tt x Tt: Row headers T, t; Column headers T, t; Cells: TT, Tt, Tt, tt.
common_errors: Used criss-cross method instead of Punnett square
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Many candidates drew the Punnett square. A few used a criss-cross method to answer.

marking_schemes.question_text: In Mendel's experiments, tall pea plants (T) are dominant over dwarf pea plants (t). What is the phenotypic ratio and genotypic ratio of the above cross in (ii) (Tt x Tt)?
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Phenotypic ratio – 3 : 1; Genotypic ratio – 1 : 2 : 1
marking_schemes.model_answer: Phenotypic ratio: 3:1 (3 tall : 1 dwarf). Genotypic ratio: 1:2:1 (1 TT : 2 Tt : 1 tt).
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Most candidates wrote phenotypic ratio and genotypic ratio of the above cross correctly.

marking_schemes.question_text: In Mendel's experiments, tall pea plants (T) are dominant over dwarf pea plants (t). State Mendel's Law of Dominance.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Out of a pair of contrasting characters, the one that is expressed is dominant and the one that is not expressed is recessive.
key_points: out of a pair of contrasting characters
the one not expressed is recessive
marking_schemes.model_answer: Out of a pair of contrasting characters, the one that is expressed is dominant and the one that is not expressed is recessive.
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Majority of the candidates stated Mendel's Law of Dominance correctly.

marking_schemes.question_text: In Mendel's experiments, tall pea plants (T) are dominant over dwarf pea plants (t). What is a Dihybrid Cross?
marking_schemes.scheme_text: It is breeding plants taking two pairs of contrasting characters.
key_points: breeding / cross involving two pairs of contrasting characters
marking_schemes.model_answer: A Dihybrid Cross is a cross between two organisms that involves two pairs of contrasting characters.
common_errors: Confusing it with Monohybrid cross
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Most candidates could explain Dihybrid cross. However, a few confused it with Monohybrid cross.

marking_schemes.question_text: Given below is a diagram representing a stage during the mitotic cell division (chromosomes being pulled to opposite poles with centrioles and asters visible). Identify the stage by giving a suitable reason.
marking_schemes.correct_answer: Anaphase; Chromatids are being pulled towards the opposite poles.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Anaphase; Chromatids are being pulled towards the opposite poles.
key_points: chromatids being pulled towards opposite poles
marking_schemes.model_answer: The stage is Anaphase. The reason is that chromatids are being pulled towards the opposite poles.
common_errors: Could identify the stage but could not give a valid reason
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Majority of candidates could identify the stage during the mitotic cell division correctly but could not give a valid reason.
marking_schemes.topic: Structure of chromosomes, Cell cycle and cell division

marking_schemes.question_text: Given below is a diagram representing a stage during the mitotic cell division. Is it a plant or an animal cell? Give a reason to support your answer.
marking_schemes.correct_answer: Animal cell; Cell wall is absent, centrioles are present, asters are present.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Animal cell; Cell wall is absent, centrioles are present, asters are present.
marking_schemes.model_answer: It is an Animal cell because the cell wall is absent, and centrioles and asters are present.
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: This part of the question was answered correctly by most candidates.
marking_schemes.topic: Structure of chromosomes, Cell cycle and cell division

marking_schemes.question_text: Given below is a diagram representing Anaphase during the mitotic cell division in an animal cell. Draw a neat, labelled diagram of the stage which follows the one shown in the diagram.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Diagram of Telophase in animal cell showing: Chromosome, Nuclear Membrane, Centriole, Aster, Furrow.
key_points: nuclear membrane forming around chromosomes at each pole
marking_schemes.model_answer: Draw Telophase of an animal cell showing two groups of chromosomes at opposite poles, nuclear membrane re-forming around each group, centrioles, asters, and a cleavage furrow developing in the middle. Label: Chromosome, Nuclear Membrane, Centriole, Aster, Furrow.
common_errors: Did not show daughter nuclei with nuclear membrane in Telophase diagram
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Many candidates did not draw the correct diagram of Telophase. Daughter nuclei with nuclear membrane was not shown.
marking_schemes.topic: Structure of chromosomes, Cell cycle and cell division

marking_schemes.question_text: Given below is a diagram representing a stage during the mitotic cell division showing 4 chromosomes in the cell. How many chromosomes will each daughter cell have after the completion of the above division?
marking_schemes.model_answer: Each daughter cell will have 4 chromosomes.
common_errors: Writing 46 instead of 4 (did not observe the diagram)
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Majority of the candidates wrote 46 chromosomes instead of 4 as they did not observe the diagram properly.
marking_schemes.topic: Structure of chromosomes, Cell cycle and cell division

marking_schemes.question_text: Given below is a diagram representing a stage during the mitotic cell division. Name the four nitrogenous bases.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Adenine, Thymine, Cytosine, Guanine.
marking_schemes.model_answer: Adenine, Thymine, Cytosine, Guanine
common_errors: Writing Thiamine and Adenosine as incorrect answers
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Most candidates named the four nitrogenous bases correctly. A few wrote Thiamine and Adenosine as incorrect answers.
marking_schemes.topic: Structure of chromosomes, Cell cycle and cell division

marking_schemes.question_text: Answer the following questions briefly: How are the cytons and axons placed in the brain and the spinal cord?
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Brain – Outer, grey matter has cytons and inner white matter has axons. Spinal Cord – Outer, white matter has axons and inner grey matter has cytons.
key_points: Brain: outer grey matter has cytons; inner white matter has axons
Spinal cord: outer white matter has axons; inner grey matter has cytons
marking_schemes.model_answer: In the brain, the outer grey matter contains cytons and the inner white matter has axons. In the spinal cord, the outer white matter has axons and the inner grey matter has cytons.
common_errors: Unsure of placement of cytons and axons in brain and spinal cord
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Most candidates wrote incorrect answers. They were unsure of the placement of cytons and axons in brain and spinal cord.

marking_schemes.question_text: Answer the following questions briefly: Which part of the human ear gives 'Dynamic balance' and 'Static balance' to the body?
marking_schemes.correct_answer: Dynamic balance – semi-circular canals/ducts/tubes; Static balance – utriculus, sacculus, utricle, saccule, vestibule
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Dynamic – semi-circular canals/ducts/tubes; Static – utriculus, sacculus, utricle, saccule, vestibule
marking_schemes.model_answer: Dynamic balance is provided by the semi-circular canals. Static balance is provided by the utriculus and sacculus (vestibule).
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Majority of the candidates answered this sub part of the question correctly.

marking_schemes.question_text: Answer the following questions briefly: Explain how the human eye adapts itself to bright light and dim light.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Bright light – Pupils constrict, Rhodopsin is bleached. Dim light – Pupils dilate, Rhodopsin is regenerated.
key_points: Bright light: pupils constrict / rhodopsin bleached
Dim light: pupils dilate / rhodopsin regenerated
marking_schemes.model_answer: In bright light, the pupils constrict and rhodopsin is bleached. In dim light, the pupils dilate and rhodopsin is regenerated.
common_errors: Did not write the role of rhodopsin for adaptation of eye
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Few candidates wrote correct answers. Many candidates did not write the role of rhodopsin for adaptation of eye.

marking_schemes.question_text: Answer the following questions briefly: What is Parthenocarpy? Give one example.
marking_schemes.scheme_text: Formation of fruit without fertilisation e.g. grapes, water melon, banana, papaya.

common_errors: Could not give a clear explanation of the term 'Parthenocarpy'
marking_schemes.examiner_notes: Most candidates could not give a clear explanation of the term 'Parthenocarpy'. However, the example was written correctly by some candidates.
